caveats: PROTOCOL.md section 13 second-host replay: established by an independent validation (VAL-20261029-7ff9db, ../../research/prime_base_oracle_tuning_20261029/validation/second-host/replay-certificate.json). The frozen holdout-P20 spec was re-executed on isolab-eks (EC2 c8a.2xlarge, AMD EPYC 9R45, L2; session ECBS1h517504d65837, ecbench 583e62f0 built from cb2ec687) with only label, measurement.rounds 2 -> 5 and measurement.isolation_required L0 -> L2 changed. All 1,008 records of ECBS1h685271327a8a have a partner with the same arm, workload, round and algorithm seed, identical in every counted, band-priced and outcome field (validator's own comparison); priced S is identical at w = 0, 0.1 and 1 on every pair; the local binary bf5eec6d replays 1,680/1,680 second-host measured runs identically; [d]G = Q holds on 2,016/2,016 second-host records under the validator's own arithmetic. The statements in replay-certificate.json and validator-report.json that no second-host replay exists predate this and are superseded by it.

Form of the second-host replay: a new session from the frozen spec matched record by record to the original, plus a local `ecbench verify --replay-all` of the new session; not an `ecbench verify --replay-all` receipt of the original session's bytes produced on the second host. `ecbench claim build --independent-receipt` (vs_rho claims) would need that form. The second-host binary's source revision is attested by its image (build-info.json), not rebuilt by the validator.

replay_certificate above is the same-host, same-binary replay (env class ECBENV3hc4d998f5ae3f); the second-host replay is a different host class and ecbench build. Neither is an independent implementation: both hosts ran ecbench. The validators' own [d]G = Q checks and stdlib recomputes are the implementation-independent checks.

The second host's older build does not emit the bitop/v1 `work` block or phase `work_native`, so no bitop/v1 figure is covered by the second-host replay. Wall times differ by host and are not compared.

The second-host session's rounds 3-5 (144 extra target-round pairs per arm on the same curve, seeds the original never ran) are post-freeze data. Over its 240 pairs sel/inc is 0.836 [0.806, 0.866], 0.817 [0.786, 0.847] and 0.746 [0.714, 0.779] at w = 0, 0.1 and 1, consistent with the frozen 96-pair reading; the decision-bearing numbers remain the frozen holdout's (gae_band and paired_ratio_sums above).

One fresh holdout curve at 20 bits (icv1-fp20-tm565-6d7d1d32, log2 r = 19.62); 48 targets x 2 rounds. The interval covers target-to-target variation on that curve only, not curve-to-curve variation. No exponent, pooled or other-size claim.

Counted unit only: ecbench GAE / sqrt(r), with unpriced native work priced at w = 0, 0.1, 1 (section 5a). At w = 0 the IC arms are lower bounds (`lower_bound: true`). No wall-clock claim; wall ratios in the compare files are L0 and descriptive.

The 20-bit holdout gain (18.2% at w = 0, 27.4% at w = 1) is larger than PROTOCOL.md section 10 prediction 4 ('any holdout gain is under about 10%'); the README does not mention the prediction. The train sweep already showed it (mitm2 n45 vs n32 at w = 0.1: 11.24 vs 13.92). Not a decision criterion; recorded as an unexpected observation.
